finding.hsts_preload.no_subdomains: HSTS without includeSubDomains: subdomains remain exposed to downgrade to HTTP.
finding.hsts_preload.not_preloaded: The HSTS header meets the preload list requirements, but the domain is not registered there (hstspreload.org).
finding.hsts_preload.preload_unready: The preload directive is present but not enough: the list requires a max-age of at least one year and includeSubDomains.
hsts_preload.score_preloaded: Domain is in the browsers' preload list
module.hsts_preload.checks: Analyses the Strict-Transport-Security header (duration, subdomains, preload directive, A to F grade) and checks whether the domain is in the browsers' HSTS preload list (hstspreload.org).
module.hsts_preload.fix:
Check that the whole site answers over HTTPS with a valid certificate and that port 80 redirects to HTTPS with a `301` redirect to the same host name: HSTS is ignored on an HTTP response.
In the web server, reverse proxy or CDN configuration, send the `Strict-Transport-Security` header on every HTTPS response (see the snippet). If the site is behind Cloudflare, use its HSTS setting (SSL/TLS, Edge Certificates) with the same values. If you have never used HSTS, start with `max-age=300` and raise it step by step up to `31536000` (one year).
Add `includeSubDomains` only after checking that every subdomain (intranet, staging and old applications included) answers over HTTPS with a valid certificate: otherwise browsers that received the header will refuse to open them.
To aim for preloading, switch to `max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload` (two years) and also send this header on any HTTPS redirect of the base domain (for example from `https://example.com` to `https://www.example.com`).
Submit the domain at hstspreload.org only when everything is ready and will last: inclusion is hard to undo, and a removal takes months to reach browsers. The list covers the base domain and all its subdomains.
Check: `curl -sI https://example.com | grep -i strict-transport-security` must show the expected value; after submission, check the domain status at hstspreload.org, then run the scan again.
module.hsts_preload.fix_snippet:
# nginx
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;

# Apache
Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"

# IIS
<configuration>
  <system.webServer>
    <httpProtocol>
      <customHeaders>
        <add name="Strict-Transport-Security" value="max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" />
      </customHeaders>
    </httpProtocol>
  </system.webServer>
</configuration>

# Caddy
example.com {
    header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
}
module.hsts_preload.title: HSTS and preload
module.hsts_preload.why: HSTS forces the browser to use HTTPS only and blocks downgrade attacks. Preloading protects even the very first visit, before the header could be received.
